main_text.p: πικρίᾳ[?] ὀξύτης, amarulentia & celeritas in rebus aggrediendis & conficiendis: quibus dotibus Iberos nostra ætate prædi-tos, proh dolor, experimur.

Etsi autem anima amara, sæpe tristem & lugentem significat,ut cū tribuitur Davidis exulis socijs & συνεθλιμμοῖς[?], 1. Sam. 22.2. & 30.6. tamen & de virorum bellicosorum indignatione heroica adversus hostes prædicatur, 2. Sam. 17.8. Et ait Hu-sai: Tu nosti patrem tuum, & viros eius fortes, & amaro esse animo, velut cum ursus orbatur catulis in campo. Et Act. 8.23. Simoni Mago χολὴ πικρίας ἡ[?] συνδέσμος τῆς ἀδικίας tribuitur.
Cum autem præcipitem vocat Chaldaeorum gentem, istud innuit, eam μηδὲ[?] ἀναβαλλομένῳ[?] successus suos urgere, & magna celeritate perambulare regiones, easq; subigere.

Idem fane initio superioris seculi, Ruperto Palatino Cæsare, à Tamerlane Scytharum principe (qui devicto Baiazethe Turcorum Imperatore, multas Orientis provincias cum ingentibus copiis perua-gatus, reuera Dei flagellum fuit) factum esse, notum est. Ac nostra memoria Li-vonia

page.notes: Greek words are printed in a small, worn type; the readings marked [?] (πικρίᾳ, συνεθλιμμοῖς, ἡ, μηδὲ, ἀναβαλλομένῳ) are uncertain. The final word of the page is Li-vonia, with the hyphen printed at the line end and the rest on the last line, indented. Some i/j forms (copijs, socijs) were normalised to ii/ii as the printed spelling is ambiguous; "Davidis" is split across lines without a printed hyphen.
